The extremal construction showing tightness is the family of all k‑edges intersecting a fixed set of \(s-1\) vertices. In this hypergraph the \(s-1\) vertices in the fixed set have degree \(\binom{n-1}{k-1}\), while every other vertex has degree exactly \(\binom{n-1}{k-1}-\binom{n-s}{k-1}\). Thus the \((s-1)\)‑st largest degree exceeds the threshold, yet the hypergraph has no matching of size \(s\). Consequently the smallest index \(m\) for which the condition \(d_m>\binom{n-1}{k-1}-\binom{n-s}{k-1}\) guarantees an \(s\)-matching must be \(m=s\).  

**Answer:** \(m = s\)  

ANSWER: s
